newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Stocks Hotels jumps on listing.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Stocks Hotels jumps on listing.

text.p: Shares in South African leisure group Stocks Hotels & Resorts Ltd roared ahead on Monday as the firm made its debut appearance on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, analysts said.
The share price quickly moved ahead from its issue price of 250 cents to hit a high of 320 cents. By 1000 GMT the stock had fallen back slightly to 290 cents.
Analysts said the firm's listing offer had been heavily oversubscribed as investors wanting to get into the tourist market are faced with a paucity of available stocks.
"There are so few tourism counters for people to invest in that Stocks Hotels was bound to create a lot of interest," said one analyst who declined to be named.
The listing injects 112 million rand of fresh cash into the company and gives it a market capitalisation of around 250 million rand.
"We are pleased with the uptake in shares and see it as a vote of confidence," said group executive chairman Bart Dorrestein.

A block of eight million shares has also been placed at a discounted premium with four black empowerment groups. They are Letsha Investment Ltd, Sedimoza Ltd, Western Cape Consortium and Western-Eastern Cape Black Empowerment Consortium.
Parent firm construction group Stocks & Stocks Ltd has retained a 40.33 percent stake.
The separate listing is aimed at strengthening the hotel unit's balance sheet and allowing it to focus on its own concerns.
Analysts said the firm had an impressive list of assets, which includes three properties in the Pilanesberg National Park north of Johannesburg and the PortsWood hotel in Cape Town.
But some expressed concern that the northern Johannesburg suburb of Sandton, where the flagship Michelangelo hotel is situated, might soon suffer from overcapacity.
"My only concern is about their forecasts for the Michelangelo. They could be too optimistic given the development going on in Sandton," one analyst said.
The company also has ambitions to enter the gambling industry as new legislation allows South Africa's provinces to offer casino licences for tender.

Stocks Hotels has said it will bid for 10 licenses, focusing on the Western Cape province. Analysts said such a strategic move was encouraging, but would bring only long-term gains as the bids process is expected to be lengthy.
Excluding the boon of securing gambling licenses, the hotels group also expects earnings to grow by some 25 percent a year.
